title: FTC Sends $23.8 Million to Grubhub Drivers and Diners in Settlement Payouts
excerpt: More than 640,000 consumers will receive checks or PayPal payments after the federal agency found Grubhub engaged in deceptive advertising and unlawful business practices.
body:
• The FTC is distributing more than $23.8 million to 640,038 affected Grubhub drivers and diners as part of a December 2024 settlement.
  • Grubhub was found to have deceived drivers about earnings, misled diners about delivery costs, blocked user accounts, and listed restaurants without consent.
  • The original judgment was $140 million, but was partially suspended because Grubhub could not pay the full amount, resulting in a $25 million settlement.
  • Recipients must cash checks within 90 days or redeem PayPal payments within 30 days to claim their refund.

The Federal Trade Commission announced on August 12 that it is sending more than $23.8 million in refund payments to drivers and diners harmed by Grubhub's deceptive business practices — the culmination of a multi-year investigation into one of America's largest food delivery platforms.

The payouts go to 640,038 affected consumers who will receive either checks in the mail or PayPal payments. Check recipients have 90 days to cash them, while PayPal recipients must redeem within 30 days.

What Grubhub Did Wrong

The FTC and Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul filed their complaint in December 2024, alleging that Grubhub engaged in a sweeping pattern of unlawful practices. The charges included deceiving drivers about how much money they would earn delivering food, misleading diners about the true cost of delivery, blocking consumers from accessing their accounts and funds, and listing restaurants on its platform without their knowledge or consent.

https://x.com/chicagotribune/status/2088063440879260123

"Grubhub tricked its customers, deceived its drivers, and unfairly damaged the reputation and revenues of restaurants that did not partner with Grubhub — all in order to drive scale and accelerate growth."

— Lina M. Khan, former FTC Chair

In some cases, restaurants were listed on the app over their explicit objections, causing reputational harm when orders went unfulfilled or were handled improperly.

The Settlement Terms

The original monetary judgment against Grubhub was $140 million, but the amount was partially suspended after the company demonstrated it could not pay the full sum. The final settlement required Grubhub to pay $25 million, with $24.8 million going to consumer restitution and $200,000 funding the Illinois Attorney General's consumer education and enforcement operations.

Beyond the financial penalty, Grubhub was ordered to make substantial operational changes. The company must now disclose the full cost of delivery upfront to consumers, honestly advertise driver pay, provide a mechanism for users to dispute blocked accounts, and list restaurants only with their explicit consent.

How to Claim Your Refund

Most eligible consumers will receive a check in the mail. Those who receive PayPal payments should watch for a notification from the platform. The FTC cautioned that it never requires people to pay money or provide account information to receive a payment — a warning aimed at preventing scams that often follow large-scale refund distributions.

Consumers with questions can contact the refund administrator, Analytics Consulting LLC, at 1-888-446-4992 or visit the FTC website for frequently asked questions about the process.

Broader Impact on Gig Economy

The settlement is part of a broader FTC crackdown on deceptive practices in the gig economy. In 2025, FTC actions led to more than $435 million in consumer redress nationwide. The Grubhub case sends a clear signal to delivery platforms and gig-economy companies that misleading pricing, inflated earnings claims, and unauthorized business listings carry serious financial and regulatory consequences.

Grubhub, which is owned by Amsterdam-based Just Eat Takeaway, denied wrongdoing in the case but agreed to settle, stating the resolution was "in the best interest" of the company.
